thread.title: What Ring Means Amazon’s Stock

author: Teresa Rivas and Jon Swartz
title: What Ring Means Amazon’s Stock
text:
Amazon.com (AMZN) is higher on Wednesday, following its announcement that it will buy security and doorbell camera maker Ring for more than $1 billion. It's the e-commerce giant's second purchase in the home-security space recently, following its acquisition of Blink , which makes smart doorbells.
Illustration: Bloomberg News It also marks the second-largest deal in Amazon’s history, behind the $13.5 billion it paid for Whole Foods Market.
Loop Capital's Anthony Chukumba reiterated his Buy rating and $1,600 price target on Amazon today, writing that Ring looks like a valuable asset for the firm: Its products are not only for sale at Amazon but also at a number of big-box retailers, including Best Buy (BBY), Target (TGT), and Walmart (WMT), and it has garnered more than $200 million of equity funding from many high-profile investors including Goldman Sachs Group (GS) and Virgin Group founder Richard Branson .
As for what it brings to the table for Amazon, Chukumba writes that Ring, like the Amazon Key Home Kit smart lock, is part of the company's plan to reduce the customer “pain point” of package theft and also add to its smart-home merchandise portfolio. He notes that Amazon's huge cash reserves means that it's able to make strategically important acquisitions, but he doesn't expect the Ring deal to have an impact on near-term financials.
Other analysts are also praising the deal. "Amazon, in essence, is building a smart-home products company to compete with hardware from Apple [AAPL], Alphabet [GOOGL], and smart-home start-ups," says Frank Gillett , principal analyst at Forrester . He doesn't expect the company to make acquisitions in makers of more-traditional home equipment, but he sees it potentially making more deals with successful start-ups with distinct smart products.
Daniel Ives , head of technology research at GBH Insights , says the acquisitions of Blink and now Ring, leveraged with its Alexa voice-activated digital assistant , demonstrate Amazon's "aggressive initiative to build out its smart-home ecosystem in 2018” in pursuit of what Ives estimates will be a $20 billion market over the next three years.
Amazon is also turning up the heat by offering Whole Foods discounts to Prime credit-card holders and making waves in the delivery space after announcing it will launch its own limited delivery service . Investors seem happy with the company's moves, sending the shares up more than 30% this year, meaning it could beat Apple and become the first company with a $1 trillion market valuation .
Amazon shares are up 0.64% in morning trading, to $1521.65.
